correctness.rationale: For each fixed radius the complete sliding-window average of a valley sequence is valley-shaped because the increment is f[x+r+1]-f[x-r], which changes sign from negative to positive at most once. The proof treats truncated graph balls: a left-truncated ball at middle center j is reproducible as a centered ball from any earlier i, and similarly right clipping from later k, proving global quasiconvexity Mf(j)<=max(Mf(i),Mf(k)) for i<j<k. Endpoint prefix and suffix means are themselves valley-shaped sequences, hence Mf(0)=max(f0,mu) and Mf(n-1)=max(f(n-1),mu); every vertex permits full mean mu. Therefore Var(Mf)<= (A-t)_++(B-t)_+, where A=f0-h, B=f(n-1)-h, t=mu-h >=(A+B)/n. The algebra gives coefficient (1-1/n), explicit sharp deficit [min((n-1)A,B)+min((n-1)B,A)]/n; equality only constant-baseline one-endpoint spike, with two equal endpoint spikes attaining the deficit. Domain arbitrary n>=3 and nonnegative one-trough real profiles (including plateaus). Independently checked 4,332 exact rational short profiles n=3..8, amplitudes 0..3; finite tests do not establish all-n theorem.
residual_risks: No theorem for arbitrary oscillatory path functions; full conjecture is open.
Shape argument depends on graph-ball endpoint truncation and count measure, not arbitrary weighted graphs.
